messages:
Maria (DevEx): Hey team — hitting a behavior in the Python async SDK when the service returns an ambiguous Content-Type. The response is JSON but Content-Type is application/octet-stream. SDK tries json() and throws JSONDecodeError and we lose status/request-id.

Maria (DevEx): Minimal repro (async):

```
async with RedwoodClient() as c:
    try:
        await c.responses.create(prompt="bad")
    except Exception as e:
        # e currently is a JSONDecodeError from aiohttp, not our SDK error
        print(repr(e))
```

Maria (DevEx): Example response (raw):
headers: {"Content-Type": "application/octet-stream", "x-request-id": "r123"}
body: b'{"error":"validation","message":"invalid prompt","request_id":"r123"}'

Joel (py-sdk): Thanks — can you confirm whether this happens with both sync and async clients or only async? Also which aiohttp version?

Maria (DevEx): Only saw it in async so far. aiohttp 3.8.4. Sync client seems to use requests and returns bytes which we include on error.

Sam: We should handle this defensively: if headers indicate non-json but body starts with b'{' or b'[' then try json parse and attach parsed payload to the SDK exception. Also always attach raw_body (bytes) and headers to the exception so callers can introspect.

Joel (py-sdk): Agreed. Proposal: SDKError fields = status, headers (dict), raw_body (bytes), parsed_error (dict|string|null). Preserve original exception as __cause__ for tracebacks. Also add a helper .json_or_text() on the response object.

Maria (DevEx): One more gotcha: sometimes body is not utf-8 and .text() raises UnicodeDecodeError. We should keep raw bytes and avoid calling .text() in exception path.

ci-bot: Created issue RED-4287: "py-sdk: preserve raw response on ambiguous Content-Type and avoid json-only parsing". Assigned to Joel (py-sdk).

Joel (py-sdk): I'll push a PR with unit + integration tests that stub a server returning application/octet-stream but JSON body. Plan: include a test that asserts exception.raw_body == body_bytes and exception.parsed_error['request_id'] == 'r123'. Target release 0.8.7.

Sam: pls add a short changelog note and a short doc blurb in errors.md about "raw_body available on exceptions".

Maria (DevEx): Thanks — this was causing data loss in our eval harness. Appreciate the quick follow-up :thumbsup:

Joel (py-sdk): Will update the PR link once open.
